nonit.name: My job isn't in IT

data.t: Clerical jobs have the highest exposure to generative AI. Most jobs are expected to change rather than disappear.
data.s: International Labour Organization (ILO), Generative AI and jobs: a 2025 update

data.t: Cashiers, administrative assistants and other clerical roles are among the fastest-declining jobs.
data.s: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025

data.t: US forecast 2025–35: cashier jobs −6.5% and about 141,800 fewer customer service representatives, partly due to AI and automation.
data.s: BLS projections, summarised by the Japan Institute for Labour Policy and Training

general.h: More jobs are being created than lost, but many will change
general.t: By 2030, global trends including AI are expected to create about 170 million jobs and displace about 92 million, a net gain of about 78 million.
general.s: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025

general.h: Employers will retrain, and some will cut
general.t: 77% of employers plan to upskill their staff, while about 41% plan to reduce their workforce as AI automates some tasks. Nearly 40% of job skills are expected to change by 2030.
general.s: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025

general.h: Most jobs will be changed by AI, not removed
general.t: One in four workers worldwide is in a job with some exposure to generative AI. Because human input is still needed, most jobs are expected to be transformed rather than made redundant.

general.h: More job ads now ask for AI skills
general.t: In 2025, 2.5% of all US job postings mentioned AI skills, up 55% from the year before.
general.s: Stanford AI Index Report 2026 (job-postings data by Lightcast)

general.h: India: tech hiring continues, but slower than revenue
general.t: In FY26, India's tech industry revenue grew 6.1% while its workforce grew only 2.3%. More than 2 million professionals were upskilled in AI.
general.s: NASSCOM Annual Strategic Review 2026 (reported by YourStory)

general.t: NASSCOM warned that as AI takes over routine work, India risks a workforce that relies on AI without deep technical skills.
general.s: NASSCOM, The State of AI-Native Talent in India (reported by YourStory)
